proposition: The positional analysis results in different classifications of Indus signs: signs can be classified as Initial, Early-Medial, Mid-Medial, Late-Medial, or Terminal; doubling, mirroring, hatching, or marking an Indus sign can change its positional classification, most likely indicating a different function or semantic value of the modified sign; and signs 382, 790, 832, and 892 are good candidates for syllabic signs, because logograms and grammatical markers should be found in restricted syntactic positions while syllables should have an almost constant positional distribution.
